Brand guidelines · Version 1.0 · October 2026

Knock on the right door.

How Knock looks, sounds and behaves. A private career service for MBA and product candidates in India, written like a letter, not a product launch.

Airmail letter conceptPowder blueNavyOne red stamp
01

Brand story and positioning

Most people apply through portals and wait. Knock does the slower, more human thing: it finds the right people at a candidate's target companies, learns about each one, and writes to them as one person to another.

What Knock is

A premium, human, tech-enabled service. Think of a private career concierge. We find hiring managers, team members, alumni and senior connectors at the companies a candidate wants to join, research each one, find a genuine shared reason to talk, write a personal first message and guide every reply. The candidate approves every message.

For
MBA graduates and people moving into product management in India.
Promise
Interviews through the people who work at your target companies.
Quality
Sixty hand-picked people a week, not thousands.
Measure
Interviews per 100 targeted prospects.
Tagline
Knock on the right door.

  • Service first

    Knock is a service delivered by people. Technology is how we deliver it, never the headline. The words for it are concierge, researched, by hand.

  • Quality over volume

    A short list of the right people beats a long list of anyone. We would rather send fewer messages that each deserve a reply.

  • The candidate stays in charge

    Every message is approved before it is sent. Nothing goes out in a candidate's name without their yes.

  • Honest about results

    We do not pad lists, promise outcomes, or quote numbers we have not measured. Specific beats impressive.

The letter metaphor

Every Knock touchpoint is a piece of mail that arrived on purpose. Powder-blue airmail paper, navy ink, one red stamp, a postmark that says where it came from. The metaphor is the reason for each design choice and the test for new ones: would this belong on a good letter?

02

Voice and tone

Knock sounds like a thoughtful person who has read about you and has something specific to say. Calm, specific, human.

Calm

No urgency tricks, no hype. Short sentences. We never shout, and we never promise what we cannot control.

Specific

Name the company, the role, the shared school. A concrete detail replaces an adjective every time.

Human

Write as one person to another. Use "we" and "you". Say "write", not "generate". Say "person", not "lead".

Hard rules

  • No em dashes. Use a full stop, a comma or a colon.
  • No exclamation marks, anywhere.
  • Sentence case for headlines. Full stops are fine on headlines.
  • No invented testimonials, statistics or logos. If we have not measured it, we do not say it.
  • AI is never the headline. If it must be mentioned, it comes late and plainly.
  • Prices are in rupees and shown upfront.

Words we do not use

AI-poweredrevolutionaryguaranteedgame-changingcutting-edgesuperchargehackunlock10xblastleadsautomation

"Guaranteed" is banned because we do not guarantee outcomes. If a reply promise exists, it states exactly what we will do and what we will not.

Say it like this

Not thisOur revolutionary AI-powered platform guarantees interviews!
ThisWe find the people who hire for your target roles, and write to each one by hand.
Not thisUnlock 10x more leads with automated outreach.
ThisSixty carefully chosen people a week. You approve every message.
Not thisApply smarter. Land your dream job faster!
ThisStop applying. Start conversations.
Not thisOur AI crafts hyper-personalised messages at scale.
ThisEach message starts from something you genuinely share with the person reading it.

Tone by moment

MomentToneExample
Website and adsPlain, confident, slightly wryJob portals are a queue. People hire people.
First client emailWarm, organisedHere is what happens in the next seven days, and what we need from you today.
A message needs approvalBrief, respectfulYour draft to the product manager at Zepto is ready. Read it, change anything, then approve.
Slow resultsHonest, practicalTwo replies so far. Here is what we are changing for next week.
03

Logo

The mark is a postage stamp carrying a door knocker. The wordmark pairs the stamp with Knock set in Archivo Extra Condensed ExtraBold. Text in the logo files is converted to outlines, so no font is needed to use them.

Use the wordmark for headers, signatures and documents. Use the stamp on its own for avatars, social marks and as the one red element in a layout.

Stamp on blue
Reversed wordmark
One colour stamp
Favicon, avatar

Clear space

Keep a margin of x on every side, where x is a quarter of the stamp's width. Nothing enters the dashed area: not text, not another logo, not the edge of the page.

xxxx

Minimum size

Stamp
24px wide on screen, 10mm in print. Below that, use the favicon.
Wordmark
90px wide on screen, 25mm in print.
Favicon
16px and up. The knocker is drawn heavier so it holds at small sizes.
Tilt
The stamp may sit at 3 degrees, as on a real letter. The wordmark never tilts.

Files

SVG masters and 512px and 1024px PNG exports are in the logo folder: knock-wordmark, knock-stamp, knock-stamp-mono, knock-favicon.

Misuse

Do not stretch or squash.

Do not recolour the stamp. It is always postal red.

Do not tilt the wordmark.

No glows, bevels or hard shadows.

Do not place the logo on a colour that hides it.

Knock

Do not retype the name in another typeface.

Contrast ratios

Computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative luminance formula. Body text needs 4.5:1 for AA and 7:1 for AAA. Large text (24px, or 19px bold) needs 3:1.

What this means

  • Navy on any blue or paper passes AAA. This is the default for text.
  • Ink 3 on the powder-blue sheet is 3.7:1. Use Ink 2 there, or keep Ink 3 for white and paper.
  • Red text on powder blue is 3.6:1. Use it for large display only, never for body or small labels.
  • Red on navy fails. In dark mode use the lighter red, 5.95:1.

05

Typography

A condensed grotesque for headlines and a serif for the words people read. Both are free from Google Fonts.

Stop applying. Start conversations.

Archivo, width 72, weight 800

Headlines, numerals, stamp lettering. Tight tracking (-0.015em), line height 0.95, sentence case. Fallback: Arial Narrow.

Archivo, width 100

UI text, labels and buttons. Small caps labels are uppercase, 600 weight, 0.12em tracking.

Source Serif 4

Body copy in letters and ledes, the address line and quotations. Italic for "To", quotes and the shared reason to talk. Fallback: Georgia.

5xl 96Knock
3xl 58The right door
xl 28Researched one at a time
lg 21We write to each person by hand.
md 18Interface and document body text.
xs 12Fold here

Scale and rules

  • Ten steps from 12px to 96px: xs, sm, base, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, 4xl, 5xl. Hero headlines use 5xl at most.
  • Body line length 45 to 62 characters. Body line height 1.55.
  • Never set body copy in the display face.
  • Headlines may carry a full stop. They never end in an exclamation mark.
  • Numerals in prices use the display face, for example Rs 2,499.
06

Motifs

Four pieces of postal furniture give Knock its character. Each one has a job. Use one or two per layout, never all four.

Stamp

The one red element. It marks the sender and the main action. Top right, tilted 3 degrees, one per layout. Never repeat it as a pattern.

Postmark

Carries the tagline in a ring: Knock on the right door. Navy at 72 per cent, multiplied over the paper, overlapping the stamp's corner, tilted -14 degrees. It says where the letter came from. Do not set it over body text.

Fold here

Perforation and fold

Dotted edges on the sheet and a dashed fold line where one zone gives way to the next. Use them to separate, never to decorate. Edges only on the largest surface in the layout.

To

Address line

An italic serif "To" and a navy rule. This is where the working action lives: a field, a name, a list of companies. It is the friendliest form of a call to action.

Restraint

  • Count the red. One stamp, plus red only for focus and a single key mark.
  • If a layout has a stamp and a postmark, drop the perforation, or the reverse.
  • Motifs sit at the edges. The middle of the page belongs to the words.
  • On dark surfaces, remove the postmark and keep the stamp.

08

Photography and illustration

Real people, real places, real paper. The imagery should feel like a private correspondence, never like a software dashboard.

Photography

  • People at work in India: a desk, a notebook, a phone mid-message, a hand with a pen.
  • Doors, thresholds, corridors, letters, envelopes and stamps. The knock is a literal image we can use.
  • Natural window light. Slightly cool, with the blues pushed toward powder blue and navy.
  • Only real clients and team members, with written consent. No invented faces presented as clients.
  • For hero use, a duotone of navy and powder blue keeps photos inside the palette.

Illustration

  • Line drawings with a 3px round-capped stroke, like the knocker on the stamp.
  • Flat fills in navy, powder blue and a single red. No gradients, no 3D.
  • Subjects: envelopes, doors, keys, stamps, route lines drawn as dashed paths.
  • Diagrams are drawn as routes and ledgers, not network graphs.

Never

RobotsGlowing brainsCircuit boardsHandshake stock photosRocket shipsChat bubble clouds

Drawn in the house style

A knocker, an envelope, a route with one red destination.

A short set of side by side checks. If a layout fails any of the right-hand examples, rework it.

Do
Stop applying. Start conversations.

We write to each person by hand.

A headline that states what we do, calm and specific.

Don't
Revolutionary AI-powered career hacks!

Unlock 10x interviews, guaranteed!

Hype words, gradients, an exclamation mark and a promise we cannot keep.

Do

One stamp. It is the sender and it is rare.

Don't

The stamp as a pattern. It stops meaning anything.

Both of you started in FMCG brand roles before moving into product. That is why we think this message is worth sending.

A real reason, in plain sentences.

Don't

10,000+ interviews booked

Invented stats and star ratings. We publish only what we have measured.
